flags.purpose: Retrieves scheduled tasks by name (supports wildcards) to locate tasks related to specific apps or scripts.
flags.security_use_case: Find PowerShell-related tasks often abused for persistence or lateral movement.
flags.threat_detected: Malicious scripts set to run at logon or intervals for persistence or C2.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Wildcards may return many results.
flags.safe_followup: Use Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for timing; inspect actions with Get-ScheduledTask | Get-ScheduledTaskAction; remove with Unregister-ScheduledTask if confirmed malicious.

flags.purpose: Retrieves tasks from a specific folder path in the scheduler namespace (must start with backslash).
flags.security_use_case: Audit Microsoft namespace for masqueraded or unauthorized tasks.
flags.threat_detected: Malware placing tasks under Microsoft paths to appear legitimate.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Correct path format required.
flags.safe_followup: Review triggers with Get-ScheduledTaskTrigger; export with Export-ScheduledTask before changes.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Shows history and next run time for enabled tasks to spot suspicious timing or failures.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect unusual execution patterns indicating compromise.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds tasks executing PowerShell with encoded arguments commonly used in fileless attacks.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect obfuscated PowerShell persistence via scheduled tasks.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Highlights non-Microsoft tasks more likely to be third-party or malicious.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identify suspicious scheduled tasks created by software or attackers.
